### TOML Configuration without Command Keys

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/api.rst

Example of configuring Cyclopts to read from a TOML file, disabling the use of command names as configuration keys.

```python
app = cyclopts.App(config=cyclopts.config.Toml("pyproject.toml", use_commands_as_keys=False))
```

### Integrating TOML Configuration with Cyclopts App

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/user_classes.rst

Configures the Cyclopts App to read parameters from a TOML file, falling back to CLI arguments when values are not found in the configuration. `use_commands_as_keys=False` ensures parameters are not nested under command names.

```python
from cyclopts import App, Parameter, config
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Annotated

app = App(
   name="movie-maintainer",
   config=config.Toml("config.toml", use_commands_as_keys=False),
)

@Parameter(name="*")
@dataclass
class Config:
   user: str
   server: str = "media.sqlite"

@dataclass
class Movie:
   title: str
   year: int

@app.command
def add(movie: Movie, *, config: Config):
   print(f"Config: {config}")
   print(f"Adding movie: {movie}")

app()
```

### Combine TOML and Environment Variable Configuration

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/config_file.rst

Configure an application to use multiple config sources by passing a sequence to App.config. Environment variables take precedence over TOML settings.

```python
# character-counter.py
import cyclopts
from pathlib import Path

app = cyclopts.App(
    name="character-counter",
    config=[
        # Since Env comes before Toml, it has priority.
        cyclopts.config.Env("CHAR_COUNTER_"),
        cyclopts.config.Toml(
            "pyproject.toml",
            root_keys=["tool", "character-counter"],
            search_parents=True,
        ),
    ],
)

@app.command

### API Reference > Config > Toml

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/api.rst

The Toml configuration class automatically reads configuration from a TOML file. It supports specifying the file path, an optional source identifier, root keys to navigate the configuration namespace, and options to enforce file existence, search parent directories, allow unknown keys, and control the use of command names as configuration keys.

--------------------------------

### API > cyclopts.config.Yaml > must_exist

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/api.rst

The `must_exist` attribute, when set to `True`, enforces that the configuration file must be present. If the file is not found, a `FileNotFoundError` will be raised.

--------------------------------

### Config Files > TOML Example

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/config_file.rst

The `Toml` configuration class allows specifying a TOML file name, root keys for namespacing, and whether to search parent directories for the configuration file. This enables setting default values for commands and their parameters directly within a `pyproject.toml` file.

--------------------------------

### API > Parameter Configuration > required

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/api.rst

The 'required' attribute indicates if a parameter must be supplied. It defaults to inferring from the function signature: False if a default value exists, True otherwise.
